sre-bot: PAGE: gpu-infra-alerts detected increased XID/driver resets on cluster-gpu-03 (severity: high)
kevin (oncall): on it. checking dashboards now. any observable customer impact?
anya (sre): seeing a spike in 5xx from /v1/generate route in us-west-2, error sig correlates with driver resets on nodes in rack-7.
devin (runtime): dumping recent container logs for affected pod set: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serving -o tail=200`
devin (runtime): logs show repeated `NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCIe Gen4) 79` and then container exit with OOM in kvcache_reclaim
kevin (oncall): paste the nvidia-smi -q output if you have it
devin (runtime): ```
Timestamp                           : Tue Apr 12 14:03:27 2026
Driver Version                      : 535.104.05
Attached GPUs                       : 1
GPU 0000:03:00.0
    Product Name                    : NVIDIA A100
    ECC Mode                        : Enabled
    ECC Errors Corrected            : 452
    ECC Errors Uncorrected          : 18
    Xid Error                        : 79
```
anya (sre): ECC uncorrectable counts rising on 3 GPUs across rack-7, looks like a transient hardware ECC surge not a single-driver regression
claudia (support): just got a customer message: "we're seeing failed requests and increased latency in our inference pipeline" — affected tenant ids: tenant-prod-alpha, tenant-ml-bench
kevin (oncall): immediate mitigation: cordon nodes in rack-7, trigger pod eviction with graceful drain window 30s, route traffic to dedicated fallback pool. I'm going to run the evacuation playbook.
devin (runtime): commands ready: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-73 && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-73 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
kevin (oncall): started cordon/drain on gpu-node-73, gpu-node-74, gpu-node-77 (these had highest uncorrectable counts). traffic-router: please shift route weight 100% away from rack-7 pools.
sre-bot: deploy-bot triggered runbook: gpu-ecc-evacuate v2. Step 1: cordon, Step 2: drain, Step 3: live migrate batch, Step 4: mark nodes for hardware triage.
deploy-bot: routing change applied: us-west-2/fallback-pool +100% for routes matching /v1/generate, expected capacity headroom +40%
anya (sre): we're seeing 200ms latency bump but 5xx rate dropping after routing change. good sign.
claudia (support): communicating to customers: "We've detected GPU hardware instability in one rack and are actively evacuating affected hosts. We've rerouted traffic and your requests should recover within minutes. We'll follow up with a postmortem"
kevin (oncall): rolling reboot not yet. prefer to evacuate and mark for hardware replacement. but let's keep nodes cordoned until hardware team signs off.
devin (runtime): aside — observed container coredump: `/var/log/pods/serving-xyz/coredump.1234` contains backtrace from kvcache allocation path. sending to SRE-artifacts.
anya (sre): creating customer impact summary for incident bridge:
- start_ts: 4999912345 (alert)
- affected_routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings (partial)
- impacted_tenants: tenant-prod-alpha, tenant-ml-bench
- mitigation: routing fallback -> +100% to fallback pool, cordon/drain rack-7 nodes, live migrate pods
- current_status: degraded -> recovery in progress
kevin (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: monitor node ECC uncorrectable counts, confirm hardware ticket #HW-8421 created and assigned, keep nodes cordoned.
anya (sre): hw ticket created: HW-8421 — requested NVML dumps and physical inspection, ETA initial triage 4h.
claudia (support): sending bulk update to affected accounts now. template: "We detected transient ECC faults in a small subset of GPUs in us-west-2. We've evacuated affected hosts and rerouted traffic; your requests should be restored. We'll follow up with more details and remediation timeline"
kevin (oncall): status update in channel in 15m. if Xid spikes restart on other racks, escalate to SEV-1.
sre-bot: automated metric alert: uncorrectable ECC count plateaued but node gpu-node-74 still reporting +3 new UEC in last 10m
devin (runtime): applied temporary qemu/firmware mitigation flags on the host to reduce ECC re-check pressure (non-invasive). documented commands in runbook.
kevin (oncall): preparing handoff: leaving this thread for next oncall. key actions pending: 1) hardware triage inspection 2) confirm replacement for 3 GPUs if uncorrectable persists 3) reconcile coredumps to root cause (kvcache OOM vs HW)
anya (sre): last check — 5xx rate down to baseline, latency back to normal, pods stable on fallback pool. marking incident as mitigated, still active for hardware follow-up.
kevin (oncall): handoff -> anyone picking this up after 18:00 UTC? @anya please take postmortem and customer follow-up.
anya (sre): will own the postmortem and customer summary. adding runbook updates to prevent blind KVCACHE OOM in future (smaller cache defaults + earlier eviction trigger).
claudia (support): copied to affected accounts and support threads.
kevin (oncall): closing paging loop here. next_message_ts: 4999912700 — followups in #hardware-triage. :white_check_mark:
